# Vercel Plugin

Give your coding agent deployment skills, framework best practices, and slash commands. Works with Claude Code, OpenAI Codex, Grok Build, Cursor, GitHub Copilot, Kimi Code, and OpenCode.

### Agent Skills

Install skills for any agent that supports them, covering Next.js, the AI SDK, Turborepo, and deploying to Vercel.

Let your agent search the docs, manage projects and deployments, and query Web Analytics through the Vercel MCP server.

### Vercel Connect

Give your agent short-lived tokens to call Slack, GitHub, Microsoft, Snowflake, or any OAuth or API-key service, and act on behalf of users, without storing provider secrets.

### Claim Deployments

### eve

Deploy and run durable backend AI agents built with eve, an open-source, filesystem-first agent framework.

### Sandbox

Run untrusted or agent-generated code in isolated, ephemeral execution environments.

### MCP Servers

### Next.js

When a team member leaves your team, Vercel deactivates any API keys they
created. If you need authentication that isn't tied to a specific person, use
OIDC tokens on Vercel
deployments.

For every option, including budgets, expiration, Token Pass keys, and keys exempt from team restrictions, see `api-keys create` in the CLI reference.

```
curl -X POST "https://api.vercel.com/v1/api-keys?teamId=$VERCEL_TEAM_ID" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $VERCEL_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{ "purpose": "ai-gateway", "name": "my-api-key" }'
```

```
curl -X POST "https://api.vercel.com/v1/api-keys?teamId=$VERCEL_TEAM_ID" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $VERCEL_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "purpose": "ai-gateway",
    "name": "my-api-key",
    "metadata": { "spendAttribution": "user" }
  }'
```

```
curl -X DELETE "https://api.vercel.com/v1/api-keys/$API_KEY_ID?teamId=$VERCEL_TEAM_ID" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $VERCEL_TOKEN"
```

The API is exposed as an HTTP/1 and HTTP/2 service over SSL. All endpoints live under the URL `https://api.vercel.com` and follow the REST architecture.

Vercel Access Tokens are required to authenticate and use the Vercel API. Include the token in the `Authorization` header:

Create and manage Access Tokens in your account settings.

By default, a request with a full-account token targets your default team. To access resources owned by another team, append the Team ID as a query string:

The API limits the number of calls you can make over a period of time. Rate limits are specified via response headers: `X-RateLimit-Limit`, `X-RateLimit-Remaining`, and `X-RateLimit-Reset`. See the limits documentation for details.

The Authorization Server API exposes a set of endpoints which are used by your application for obtaining, refreshing, revoking, and introspecting tokens, as well querying user info:

| Endpoint | URL |
| --- | --- |
| Authorization Endpoint | https://vercel.com/oauth/authorize |
| Token Endpoint | https://api.vercel.com/login/oauth/token |
| Revoke Token Endpoint | https://api.vercel.com/login/oauth/token/revoke |
| Token Introspection Endpoint |
| User Info Endpoint | https://api.vercel.com/login/oauth/userinfo |

| Parameter | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `client_id` | Yes | The ID of the App, located in the Manage page of the App. |
| `scope` | No | A space-separated list of scopes you're requesting: `openid`, `email`, `profile`, and `offline_access`. If you request `email` or `profile` and that scope isn't configured in your app's Manage settings, Vercel rejects the request. With the default `response_mode`, Vercel redirects to your `redirect_uri` with an `invalid_scope` error. If you request `offline_access` and it isn't configured, it's filtered out. If you don't pass `scope`, all scopes configured in your app are included by default. |
| `redirect_uri` | Yes | The URL used to redirect users back to the application after granting authorization, located in the Manage page of the App under Authorization Callback URLs. |
| `response_type` | Yes | Must be `code`. |
| `response_mode` | No | Specifies how the authorization response is delivered. If you omit this parameter, Vercel redirects to your `redirect_uri` with query parameters. The only value you can pass is `web_message.opener`. Vercel rejects any other value, including `query`, with an `invalid_request` error. Use `

The Token Endpoint is used to exchange the `code` returned from the Authorization Endpoint, or a Refresh Token for a new Access Token and Refresh Token pair.

| Parameter | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `grant_type` | Yes | Either `authorization_code` or `refresh_token`. - If the user signs in from the application then `authorization_code` should be used. - If the user is already signed in but the Access Token has expired, then `refresh_token` should be used. |
| `client_id` | Yes | The ID of the App located in the Manage page. |
| `client_secret` | Optional | The client secret generated in the Manage page. Omit this parameter if client authentication is set to `none`, or if you authenticate with a JWT assertion or an OIDC token using `client_assertion` and `client_assertion_type`. |
| `client_assertion` | No | Required when authenticating with `client_assertion` instead of `client_secret`. A JWT that proves the client's identity, either a JWT assertion you sign or an OIDC token from a trusted issuer. |
| `client_assertion_type` | No | Required when using `client_assertion`. Must be `urn:ietf:params:oauth:client-assertion-type:jwt-bearer` for a JWT assertion, or `urn:vercel:params:oauth:client-assertion-type:oidc-bearer` for an OIDC token. |
| `code` | No | If `grant_type` is `authorization_code` then this parameter is r

Vercel protects your projects across access, application, and infrastructure security.

Vercel access tokens authenticate requests to the Vercel REST API and the Vercel CLI on your behalf. You create and manage them on the Account Tokens page, under the Settings area of your account, and you can also create them without the dashboard using the REST API or the CLI.

| Response | Cause | Fix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `403` with `"invalidToken": true` | The token is wrong, expired, or deleted. | Check that the header reads `Authorization: Bearer <token>` and that the token still appears on the Account Tokens page. If you've lost the token, create a new one. |
| `403` with `"missingToken": true` | The request has no `Authorization` header, or the header isn't in the form `Bearer <token>`. A common cause is an environment variable that's empty in the current shell. | Check that the header reads `Authorization: Bearer <token>`. Run `echo "${VERCEL_ACCESS_TOKEN:+set}"` to confirm the variable is set, then send the request from the same shell. |
| A team's resources are missing, or the request is denied, with a full-account token | A full-account token targets your default team unless you specify a team. | Add `teamId` or `slug` to the request. |
| A project-scoped token is denied | Project-scoped tokens can't access other projects, team-level resources, or user-level resources. | Use a team-scoped token, or a project-scoped token for the project you're requesting. |
| `429` | The request exceeded a REST API rate limit. | Reduce your request rate and r

* REST API, where the create an auth token endpoint accepts an optional `projectId` in the request body to scope the token to a project.
* Vercel CLI, where `vercel tokens` manages tokens from the command line. A `vercel login` session can't create tokens, so pass an existing access token to the CLI with the `--token` option or the `VERCEL_TOKEN` environment variable. To create a project-scoped token, pass a team-scoped token for the team that owns the project and run `vercel tokens create <TOKEN_NAME> --project <PROJECT_ID>`. The command takes the team from the token's scope, so a full-account token doesn't work with `--project`.

Creating a full-account token through the CLI or API, or a team-scoped token through the API, requires a full-account token. A team-scoped token can create only project-scoped tokens for projects in its team. A
project-scoped token cannot mint new tokens.

The Get Auth Token Metadata endpoint, `GET /v5/user/tokens/{tokenId}`, returns the token's `activeAt` field, the timestamp in milliseconds of the most recent request that used the token. Pass `current` as the `tokenId` to read the metadata for the token that authenticates the request. With your token in the `VERCEL_ACCESS_TOKEN` environment variable, run:
